extraction.units: verbatim excerpts from the held windows only; every signal carries source id, exact excerpt, character offset, category and nature (EXPLICIT textual statement vs INFERRED analyst relation)
categories: CITATION-MARKER - a bracketed reference number as it literally appears
ATTRIBUTION-PHRASE - one of a CLOSED phrase list, matched case-insensitively
NAMED-AUTHORITY - a person or institution the text explicitly names as a source, author, translator or authority (the historical SUBJECT is not a source and is excluded)
NAMED-WORK-OR-BODY - a work or body of literature the text names (e.g. 'Buddhist literature', 'the present work')
QUOTATION - a quoted passage presented with an attributing frame
RELIANCE-STATEMENT - an explicit statement that the text rests on earlier translations or scholarship
extraction.explicit-vs-inferred: EXPLICIT = the words are on the page verbatim; INFERRED = an analyst relation between signals (never presented as text)
extraction.no-invention: no bibliographic detail is invented and no incomplete marker is expanded using outside knowledge
extraction.truncation-rule: absence of an attribution in a TRUNCATED window is NOT evidence that no attribution exists
extraction.subject-exclusion: Ashoka/Asoka as the historical subject is NOT a named authority; only persons/institutions named as sources count

requirements.EXPLICIT-SHARED-ATTRIBUTION: the SAME named authority or named work appears in BOTH windows as a source
requirements.POSSIBLE-SHARED-DERIVATION: a visible connection exists (same named authority/work, or both explicitly state reliance on the same named body of translations) but it is insufficient to establish a common underlying evidence base
requirements.DISTINCT-STATED-ATTRIBUTIONS: BOTH windows explicitly name at least one accountable source/authority, the named sets are DISJOINT, and each chain is reconstructable to at least one named terminal; this does NOT prove independence
requirements.ATTRIBUTION-CHAIN-INCOMPLETE: at least one window's chain has a missing link (a marker without a visible referent, an unnamed translation or writer, or a truncation cutting an attribution), so neither shared nor distinct can be established
requirements.UNKNOWN: no provenance signal in either window

classification.precedence-law: the first satisfied class wins; DISTINCT requires BOTH chains reconstructable, so an incomplete chain outranks it
forbidden-inferences: different citation numbers do not mean different sources
different intermediary sources do not prove independent underlying evidence
a common translator or historian is a provenance connection, not proof that every claim derives from that person
different publishers do not establish source independence

ceiling.independence: this experiment CANNOT promote independence to ESTABLISHED
ceiling.strongest-positive: distinct stated attribution chains (DISTINCT-STATED-ATTRIBUTIONS) - actual independence remains UNKNOWN
four-separate-propositions: independent observation of the historical facts

carry-over.a46-claims: UNCHANGED - A46's 2 AGREEMENT / 2 PARTIAL / 9 NO-MATCH stands; A47 does not re-run it
carry-over.ladder: UNCHANGED - DIVERSITY-ONLY stands unless the A46 claim layer AND independence both support otherwise; A47 cannot supply independence
carry-over.ea1: UNCHANGED - A42 PARTIAL, A43 EVIDENCE-GAP, A44 EVIDENCE-GAP

prohibitions: no modification of A42-A46 artifacts or manifests
no change to A46's comparison methodology
no production code change beyond a narrowly scoped offline test
